cells.tense: The pull is here now, and the hands are already moving with it.
cells.act: name the mechanism in one line and change nothing
cells.ask: Catch the same situation coming around, put one line down on how it works underneath, and stop there — no plan, no fixing.
cells.core:
You can watch how a situation moves under its surface, and hold that shape without pinning it to one example. There's a pull in you toward something not yet reached, and it isn't a daydream; repetitions carry it, the way a practice points at a light someone chose. What others take for a tangent, you're following the line. That work has a good place to land right now.

Let it land small. Take a pattern you've noticed running through a few recent situations, and put down how it works underneath in one plain line, then walk away and change nothing. A page like that shows whether the reading holds weight or runs ahead of what's actually here. Nothing has to be altered for the line to have done its work.

cells.tense: Tomorrow has already gone bright, and the hands are still here behind it.
cells.act: wait until you know which part matters, then begin with that part
cells.ask: Before the next thing that matters, sit still for a minute until the piece that clearly counts shows itself. Begin there, and save the rest of the plan.
cells.core:
The pull has jumped ahead of you. You're pointing at a light that hasn't arrived, and the plan ahead looks brighter than the work under it — that picture is alive, and it's real, but it sits past the step you're standing on. The pattern-watching runs forward then, and the future becomes the room you live in.

Before the next session, job, or decision, slow at the threshold and give your sense of what counts room to settle before the arms move. Begin with the piece that shows itself, and set the rest of the plan aside for now. The pushing drops off, and what's left is work you can feel under you today. The bright plan loses its glare once the next part is simply being done.

cells.tense: You waited at a door that was already behind you when you turned around.
cells.act: tend it small and ask nothing of it
cells.ask: Take a practice of yours — a few notes, a short sitting with a question — and make it smaller than feels serious, then tend it on the days it comes.
cells.core:
The pattern has been looked at and hasn't flowered. Whatever was cultivated there hasn't carried you anywhere, and that has left things thin — each instance feels separate now, and the wish underneath reads as a wall you keep approaching and not reaching. You keep to the work without being in it.

What that kind of front wants is something modest and tended, expecting nothing back. Take a small practice of yours — a few notes on how a thing works, a short sitting with a question — and make it smaller than feels serious, then tend it on the days it comes and ask it for no outcome. Don't judge whether it's working; that's for later. What gets raised without expectations returns the light to the room, and the first thing you'll notice isn't the shine — it's that you stopped tensing before it.

cells.tense: You are lighting the room from a corner of it, with your pen laid down.
cells.act: keep it at its real size when you are asked to shrink it
cells.ask: When someone asks this week what you make of a situation, give the pattern the size you actually see it — plain, untrimmed — and if they wave it off, let it stand.
cells.core:
There's a radiance in how you read a situation, and it doesn't switch off with the light. People come to you already lit, because the pattern gets found and then said. The rule you grew up under may be that naming it isn't yours, or that naming it isn't a big thing. So it stays unclaimed, and the shine behind it does too.

When the question comes, hold the pattern the size you actually see it. The next time someone asks what you make of what's going on, state it without trimming for the room, and if they wave it off, stay standing. Holding your shape when you're asked to shrink is the work, and it needs no speech. Do it plain, once, and see what you were carrying.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that a pattern the person names will land and free something — the record has the mechanism, not the outcome, so any cell that promises the seeing will liberate or that the run of days holds the shape would be mine, not theirs. A reader could reasonably say the signs are ordinary and I made a run where none exists; that's fine, because the asks ask for a small act — a minute, a page, a lifted forecast — and each stays useful even if the read is wrong: the act doesn't depend on my pattern holding. The sentence that serves me rather than them would be any version that says 'you're a seer' or names the mechanism instead of describing what a hand does — lining it out.
